methods.label: Separate the inside and outside regions
methods.explanation:
A point is visible during the walk exactly when it is within \(1\) km of some point on the square's boundary. We can find the visible areas inside and outside the square separately.

Inside, the unseen points are more than \(1\) km from every side. They form the central square with side length \(5-2=3\) km. Thus the visible interior has area
\[
5^2-3^2=16.
\]
Outside, there is a \(5\)-by-\(1\) rectangle directly beside each side. Beyond both adjacent sides at a corner, the closest boundary point is that corner, so the remaining visible piece is a quarter disk of radius \(1\). These four rectangles and four quarter disks cover the exterior visible region without overlapping interiors. The quarter disks together have the area of one unit disk, giving exterior area
\[
4(5\cdot1)+\pi\cdot1^2=20+\pi.
\]
The total is therefore
\[
16+20+\pi=36+\pi\approx39.14.
\]
Rounded to the nearest whole number, the area is \(\boxed{39}\) square kilometers, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
